subject: physiology
title: Cardiac electrophysiology, action potentials and pacemaker automatism
refs: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology

steps.tx: Ventricular and atrial working myocytes display a non-pacemaker **cardiac action potential** divided into five distinct phases from zero to four. Phase zero is rapid depolarization driven by voltage-gated sodium channels. Phase one is early transient repolarization mediated by outward potassium currents. Phase two is a prolonged plateau where inward L-type calcium currents balance outward delayed rectifier potassium currents, sustaining contraction and preventing tetanus.
steps.say: Ventricular and atrial working myocytes display a cardiac action potential divided into five distinct phases from zero to four. Phase zero is rapid depolarization driven by sodium channels. Phase one is transient repolarization. Phase two is a prolonged plateau where inward calcium currents balance outward potassium currents, sustaining contraction. Phase three is rapid repolarization.

rows: Inward Ca2+ (L-type CaV1.2) balanced by outward K+
Outward delayed rectifier K+ currents (IKr, IKs)
Inward rectifier K+ current (IK1), rests at -90 mV

steps.tx: In contrast to contractile myocytes, sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodal cells exhibit spontaneous **pacemaker automatism** lacking a stable resting potential. Phase four is characterized by slow diastolic spontaneous depolarization driven by the funny current, which conducts mixed sodium and potassium through hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels. Progressive inward funny current and T-type calcium influx gradually depolarize the membrane toward threshold.
steps.say: In contrast to contractile myocytes, nodal cells exhibit spontaneous pacemaker automatism lacking a stable resting potential. Phase four is characterized by slow diastolic depolarization driven by the funny current through hyperpolarization-activated channels. Inward funny current and T-type calcium influx depolarize the membrane toward threshold.

vis.alt: Overlaid action potentials of a sinoatrial node cell and a ventricular myocyte: the node has no stable resting potential and drifts upward in phase 4 until a slow calcium upstroke, the ventricle rests at minus 90, fires rapidly through sodium channels and holds a calcium plateau.
vis.caption: Pacemaker cells drift up by the funny current; ventricular cells snap up with sodium and plateau with calcium.

steps.tx: Autonomic innervation modulates sinoatrial node firing rate by shifting the slope of phase four depolarization. **Sympathetic stimulation** activates beta-one adrenergic receptors, raising cyclic AMP and protein kinase A, which enhances funny current and L-type calcium currents, steepening phase four slope and producing tachycardia. **Parasympathetic vagal stimulation** activates muscarinic M2 receptors and opens inward rectifier potassium channels (IKACh), hyperpolarizing nodal cells and causing bradycardia.
steps.say: Autonomic innervation modulates sinoatrial node firing rate by shifting the slope of phase four depolarization. Sympathetic stimulation activates beta-one receptors, raising cyclic AMP and steepening phase four slope to cause tachycardia. Parasympathetic vagal stimulation activates M2 receptors and opens potassium channels, causing bradycardia.

left.title: Sympathetic stimulation (Beta-1)
points: Enhances funny current (If) and L-type Ca2+ current

right.title: Parasympathetic stimulation (M2)
points: Inhibits adenylyl cyclase via Gi protein
Flattens slope of phase 4 and hyperpolarizes node

steps.tx: The prolonged **effective refractory period** of ventricular myocardium lasts throughout phases zero, one, two and mid-phase three. During this interval, voltage-gated sodium channels remain in an inactivated conformational state and cannot reopen, making it impossible to elicit another conducted action potential regardless of stimulus strength. This long refractory period prevents summation of contractions and tetanic cardiac arrest, ensuring rhythmic chamber filling and ejection.
steps.say: The prolonged effective refractory period of ventricular myocardium lasts throughout phases zero, one, two and mid-phase three. During this interval, sodium channels remain inactivated and cannot reopen, making it impossible to elicit another action potential. This prevents summation and tetanus, ensuring rhythmic cardiac pumping.
